mechanism_trace.code: SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS total_matches, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE composite_verdict = 'confirmed') AS confirmed, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE composite_verdict = 'partial') AS partial, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE composite_verdict = 'denied') AS denied, AVG(composite_score)::numeric(4,3) AS mean_composite_score FROM mimamsa_calibration WHERE chart_id = $1
mechanism_trace.bug: The FILTER clauses compare composite_verdict against lowercase literals 'confirmed'/'partial'/'denied', but the live mimamsa_calibration.composite_verdict column stores UPPERCASE values 'CONFIRMED'/'PARTIAL'/'REFUTED'/'UNRESOLVED' (verified via direct DB query). 'denied' also does not match the real label 'REFUTED' at all, even case-corrected. Postgres string comparison is case-sensitive and exact, so all three FILTER predicates always evaluate to zero matches regardless of real data — total_matches (a plain COUNT(*) with no verdict filter) is the only correct number in the block.
